title: Add KMS provenance tagging, audit log signing, and RBAC v2 shadow rollout for region pinning
author: Maya Patel
release_notes:
- Introduces KMS provenance tagging on wrapped keys for better auditability.
- Adds cryptographic signing of service-level audit export payloads.
- Enables RBAC v2 in shadow mode for region pinning policies (no enforced deny).
- Backwards-compatible feature flags and migration steps included.
description:
Motivation: Customers operating under data residency and compliance constraints require stronger assurances about where encryption keys originate and that audit exports cannot be tampered with in transit. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: (1) KMS provenance metadata attached to key-wrapping operations so we can assert origin and region affinity; (2) signing of audit export bundles at the service edge to provide an integrity stamp for downstream collectors; (3) a controlled rollout of RBAC v2 region-pinning policies using a shadow mode so we can validate policy coverage without impacting production traffic.

Summary of changes: Added provenance metadata to the KMS proxy and key-wrapping paths, introduced an audit-signing layer that signs compressed audit bundles with a service key, and implemented RBAC v2 policy evaluation in shadow mode for region pinning (results logged but not enforced). Feature gates have been added to enable full enforcement only after a canary and a controlled policy rollout.

Design notes: 1) KMS provenance: the KMS proxy now attaches a compact provenance claim to every wrapped key: origin_region, kms_cluster_id, and wrap_timestamp. These entries are persisted to the existing key-metadata store and surfaced in the audit logs. The provenance payload is intentionally minimal and canonicalized for downstream indexing. 2) Audit signing: on export we compute a SHA256 over the newline-delimited audit records, compress with gzip, then sign with a service-level ED25519 key stored in the platform KMS. The signature is appended as a header on the export bundle and recorded as a separate entry in the audit index to enable verifier workflows. 3) RBAC v2 shadow rollout: the policy evaluator has been extended to evaluate the new region-pinning RBAC rules, emitting an explicit "shadow_decision" trace to logs and to the SLO tracing pipeline. Enforcement is disabled by default and gated by the feature flag "rbac_v2_region_pin_enforce".

Operational considerations: - Feature flags: rbac_v2_region_pin_shadow (on by default in staging), rbac_v2_region_pin_enforce (off by default). - Migration: a data migration migrates a small number (~300k) of key-metadata rows to attach provenance claims; migration is idempotent and bounded. - Backwards compatibility: older clients ignore provenance metadata. Audit consumers can opt-in to verify signatures; verification tools included in this PR can run standalone without enforcement. - Performance: audit signing adds ~4-8ms to export path under typical batch sizes; added benchmark results in the PR.

Testing and validation: unit tests for KMS proxy provenance, end-to-end test that verifies signed export round-trip + verifier, and integration tests for RBAC v2 evaluator in shadow mode. Load testing against canary showed no regression beyond the expected signing overhead. A staged canary in us-west-2 (5% traffic) was used to validate production telemetry and false-positive counts before full enablement.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main with feature gates off for enforcement. 2) Enable rbac_v2_region_pin_shadow in staging (done) and monitor shadow_decision rates and false positives for 72h. 3) Run provenance migration in a read-only window for metadata sync; verify via sampling queries. 4) Enable audit verifiers in downstream collectors and validate signatures on archived bundles. 5) Toggle rbac_v2_region_pin_enforce in a progressive canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) after two successful days of no high-severity findings.

Checklist: [x] Tests added/updated [x] Migration script included [x] Feature flags added [x] Benchmarks attached [x] Docs note for operators [x] Linear/Jira links included

If any concerns about signature key management exist we can alternate to HSM-backed signing (KMS-as-HSM) as a follow-up; current implementation uses service-level ED25519 keys provisioned via our existing KMS plugin.
